The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Planning
Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 4th Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City at Planning@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at (626) 300­0713
prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Planning Commission
by submitting a public comment request and giving it to the Community Development Director
prior to the meeting. At this time, the public may address the Planning Commission on items
that are not on the agenda. Pursuant to state law, the Planning Commission may not discuss
or take action on issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.3).
 The Chair reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to
follow up on such items.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

1.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL FOR DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR
  21­26 AND DR 22­69 AT 1733 EUSTON ROAD TO CONSTRUCT A
  NEW TWO­STORY HOME WITH A NEW FRONT YARD WALL AND THE
  REMOVAL OF ONE HERITAGE TREE. (CHANG)
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Planning Commission: 1. Determine that
  based on the whole of the administrative record, the proposed roofing project is
  exempt from CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Section 15301, Class 3 (New
  Construction or Conversion of Small Structures), and that there is no substantial
  evidence demonstrating an exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15300.2 applies; 2. Find that the proposed project meets the
  required findings; and 3. Approve the project.

2.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL FOR DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR
  22­21 TO RECONSTRUCT THE EXISTING TWO­STORY HOME WITH
  AN ATTACHED ONE­CAR GARAGE AT 3325 MONTEREY ROAD.
  (CHENG)
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Planning Commission: 1) Determine that
  based on the whole of the administrative record, that the project is exempt from
  CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Sections 15331, 15303, and 15302, Class
  31, Class 3, and Class 2, and that there is no substantial evidence demonstrating an
  exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2
  applies; 2) Find that the proposed project meets the required findings; and 3)
  Approve the project with the added conditions: (i) that exterior conditions and
  finishes shall match the existing photos found in the Preservation Plan and any field
  changes shall be brought back to the Planning Commission for approval; and (ii) if
  mold is found on the front façade, the applicant shall contact the City and prepare
  and execute a remediation plan to eliminate or contain the mold. If the mold
  remediation requires any alteration to the front façade, the applicant must obtain
  approval for such alteration from the Planning Commission under Municipal Code
  section 23.15.09 before commencing any work to alter the front facade.

3.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL FOR DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR
  23­01, DR 23­72, & DR 23­73 AT 2221 EAST CALIFORNIA
  BOULEVARD TO CONSTRUCT A NEW TWO­STORY HOME,
  RECONFIGURING THE FRONT YARD PAVEMENT EXCEEDING 25% OF
  THE IMPERVIOUS COVERAGE, NEW FRONT YARD WALLS, AND
  REMOVAL OF (1) ESTABLISHED TREE AND (2) HERITAGE TREES.
  (ARCHIFIELD INC.)
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Planning Commission: 1) Determine that
  based on the whole of the administrative record, that the project is exempt from
  CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Sections 15331, 15303, and 15302, Class
  31, Class 3, and Class 2, and that there is no substantial evidence demonstrating an
  exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2
  applies; 2) Find that the proposed project meets the required findings; and 3)
  Approve the project with the added conditions: Should the relocated Palm Trees die,
  the City’s Urban Forester shall determine the replacement tree’s location, size, and

  NO. CUP 23­03 AT 2459 MISSION STREET UNIT B FOR THE
  OPERATION OF A YOGA STUDIO AND DETERMINATION OF
   Recommendation: Staff recommends the Planning Commission: 1) Determine that
  based on the whole of the administrative record, that the project is exempt from
  CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Sections 15331, 15303, and 15302, Class
  31, Class 3, and Class 2, and that there is no substantial evidence demonstrating an
  exception to the categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2
  applies; 2) Find that the proposed project meets the required findings; and 3)
  Approve the project with the added conditions: Should the relocated Palm Trees die,
  the City’s Urban Forester shall determine the replacement tree’s location, size, and
  species.

4.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL FOR CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT
  NO. CUP 23­03 AT 2459 MISSION STREET UNIT B FOR THE
  OPERATION OF A YOGA STUDIO AND DETERMINATION OF
  REQUIRED PARKING SPACES. (SONG)
  Recommendation: Staff recommends approval of Conditional Use Permit Case No. CUP
  23­03. If the Planning Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, then
  following the public hearing, the actions would be: 1) Pursuant to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) and the State CEQA Guidelines, the Planning
  Commission in the exercise of its independent judgment finds that Conditional Use
  Permit Case No. CUP 23­03 is categorically exempt under Section 15301, (Existing
  Facilities). 2) The Planning Commission in the exercise of its independent judgment
  hereby makes the findings listed on attached Resolution 23­12 for Conditional Use
  Permit Case No. 23­03, which are incorporated herein by this reference. 3) The
  Planning Commission approves Conditional Use Permit Case No. 23­03, subject to the
  attached conditions on Exhibit A of Resolution 23­12, all of which are incorporated
  herein by this reference.

5.  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDING
  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. O­23­1409
  ADDING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.05.03 REGARDING
  DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS AND OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS
  FOR MULTI­FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS IN THE
  HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL ZONE
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Planning Commission review and adopt
  Resolution No. PCR 23­13 recommending the City Council adopt draft Ordinance No.
  O­23­1409 adding Municipal Code Section 23.05.03 regarding development standards
  and objective design standards for multi­family residential development projects.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve the
  regular meeting of August 23, 2023.
